explanation: The capital of Syria, mentioned as a place of destruction and judgment in the book of Isaiah 17.
A city in ancient Israel, mentioned as a place where people will flee from under the destruction of Damascus.
Another name for the Northern Kingdom of Israel, used here to show that they too will suffer under God's judgment.
A reference to Israel's greatness and prosperity, which will be reduced because of their sins and disobedience toward God.
This term refers to what remains after the harvest. In this context, it means that only a small remnant of the people will survive God's judgment.
The Assyrian Empire, a powerful enemy of Israel and Judah, whom God will use as an instrument of His judgment.
A mountainous land north of Israel, known for its cedar trees. Here it symbolizes Israel's destruction, since even the mighty cedars will be cut down.
